You will summon a nation you have never known,
and a nation that never knew you will hurry to you,
because of Yahweh your God, the Holy One of Israel,
who has made you glorious.

Seek Yahweh while he lets himself be found;
call upon him while he is near.

Let the wicked forsake his way,
and the man of iniquity his thoughts;
and let him return to Yahweh, that he may have compassion on him,
and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.

For my thoughts are not your thoughts,
neither are your ways my ways, declares Yahweh.

For as the heavens are higher than the earth,
so my ways are higher than your ways,
and my thoughts than your thoughts.

For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven
and return not there, but water the earth
and make it bring forth and sprout,
and give seed to the sower and bread to the eater,{c}

so shall my word be that goes forth from my mouth;
it shall not return to me empty,
but it shall do what I desire,
and succeed in that for which I sent it.

For in joy you shall go out,
and in peace you shall be led forth;
the mountains and the hills shall break out before you into song,
and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands.

notes.text: The Great Isaiah Scroll lacks “and eat; come, buy,” probably because the copyist’s eye skipped from one “buy” to the next.
Hebrew hasde dawid hanne’emanim, “the sure acts of loyal love promised to David”; compare 2 Samuel 7:15–16. Acts 13:34 quotes the line from the Septuagint, “the holy and sure things of David.”
Compare 2 Corinthians 9:10.
Hebrew leshem, “for renown.”

verses.text:
Blessed is the man who does this,
and the son of man who holds fast to it,
who keeps the Sabbath so as not to profane it,
and keeps his hand from doing any evil.”

Let no foreigner who has joined himself to Yahweh say,
“Yahweh will surely keep me apart from his people”;
and let no eunuch say,
“Look, I am only a dry tree.”

For thus says Yahweh:
“To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths,
who choose the things in which I delight
and hold fast my covenant,

“As for the foreigners who attach themselves to Yahweh,
to serve him, to love Yahweh’s name
and to be his servants,
all who keep the Sabbath without desecrating it
and hold firmly to my covenant,

The Lord Yahweh declares,
who gathers the outcasts of Israel,
“I will yet gather others to him
besides those already gathered.”{e}

All you beasts of the field, come to devour,
all you beasts in the forest.

notes.text: The Great Isaiah Scroll begins the chapter with “For.”
Hebrew yad vashem, literally “a hand and a name.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “shall go up,” that is, “shall go up for acceptance on my altar.”
Jesus quotes the last two lines when he clears the temple (Mark 11:17; compare Matthew 21:13; Luke 19:46).
Compare John 10:16.
The written form of the Hebrew has “His watchman.”
Hebrew hozim, perhaps “panting” or “raving”; the Great Isaiah Scroll reads “they are seers” (hozim, spelled differently), a bitter play on the prophets. The Septuagint has “dreaming of rest.”
Or “are strong of appetite.”
So the Masoretic Text; the Great Isaiah Scroll reads “let us take wine.”

verses.text:
The righteous man perishes,
and no one takes it to heart;
devout men are gathered away,
while none understands
that from the face of evil
the righteous man is gathered away.

At whom do you make sport?
Against whom do you open wide the mouth
and thrust out the tongue?
Are you not a brood of rebellion,
offspring of deceit,

you who burn with lust among the oaks,{c}
under every green tree,
who slay the children in the valleys,
under the clefts of the crags?

Upon a high and lofty mountain
you have set your bed;
there also you went up
to offer sacrifice.

You went down to the king{g} with oil,
and made your ointments many;
you dispatched your messengers to distant parts,
and debased yourself as far as Sheol.

You were tired out by your long journey,
but you never said, ‘There is no use’;
you found renewed strength,
so you did not give out.

“Whom did you dread and fear,
that you lied,
and did not remember me,
nor lay it to your heart?
Have I not kept silent, and that from of old,{h}
and so you fear me not?

I will declare your righteousness and your deeds,
but they shall not profit you.{i}

When you cry for help,
let your gathered hoard rescue you!
But the wind shall lift them all away;
a breath shall take them away.
But he who takes refuge in me shall possess the land
and inherit my holy mountain.”

And one shall say,
“Build up, build up, clear the way;{j}
lift every stumbling block
out of the way of my people.”

For this is what the lofty and exalted One says,
who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy:
“I live in a high and sacred place,
yet I am also with those who are crushed and humble in spirit,
revitalizing the humble spirit
and reviving the crushed heart.
“There is no peace,” says my God, “for the wicked.”{o}

notes.text: Or “each who walks in his uprightness.”
Hebrew “and she plays the harlot.”
Or “who inflame yourselves among the terebinths” or “among the gods.”
There is a play on words in the Hebrew: helqe nahal, “smooth stones of the valley,” and helqekh, “your portion.”
Probably a pagan symbol in place of the reminder of the law commanded in Deuteronomy 6:9.
“A hand” may be a euphemism for the male member.
Hebrew melekh, or perhaps Molech (compare Leviticus 18:21).
Or, with a slight change of the Hebrew, “and hidden my eyes.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “your collection,” anticipating verse 13.
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “the highway.” Compare 40:3; 62:10.
Hebrew neshamot, “breaths,” the breath of life.
The Great Isaiah Scroll lacks “I will lead him” and reads “I will repay him with consolations.”
The written form of the Hebrew has nov, the read form niv; both mean “fruit” of the lips, that is, praise. The Great Isaiah Scroll has “peace” once.
Paul echoes this line in Ephesians 2:17.
Compare 48:22.

verses.text:
Still they look for me every day
and take delight in learning my ways,
like a nation that has done right
and has not abandoned its God’s justice;
they ask me for fair rulings
and take pleasure in coming close to God.

‘Why have we fasted,’ they say, ‘and you do not see?
Why have we humbled our souls, and you take no notice?’
See, in the day of your fast you pursue your own business,
and drive hard all your workers.{b}

See, you fast for quarrel and strife,
and to hit out with the fist of wickedness.
You do not fast as on this day
to have your voice heard on high.

Is that the sort of fast I choose,
a day when someone humbles himself?
Is it hanging your head like a reed
and spreading out sackcloth and ashes to lie on?
Do you really call this a fast,
a day Yahweh will accept?

“Is not this the fast that I choose:
to loosen the fetters of wickedness,
to untie the cords of the yoke,
to send away the crushed as free,{c}
and that you break every yoke?

Then you will call, and Yahweh will answer;
you will cry for help, and he will say, ‘Here I am.’
If you remove the yoke from among you,
the pointing finger and the malicious talk,

if you spend yourselves for the hungry
and satisfy the need of the afflicted,
your light will shine in the dark,
and your night will turn into noon.

And Yahweh will guide you always
and satisfy your soul in scorched places
and make your bones strong;
and you shall be like a watered garden,
like a spring of water
whose waters never fail.

Your people will rebuild the old ruins
and raise up foundations from past generations;
you will be known as the one who repairs gaps in walls
and restores streets to live on.

“If you turn back your foot from the Sabbath,
from doing your pleasure on my holy day,
and call the Sabbath a delight,
the holy day of Yahweh honorable,
and honor it, not going your own ways,
nor seeking your own pleasure, nor speaking idle words,

then you shall take delight in Yahweh,
and I will set you riding on the high places of the land,
and nourish you with the inheritance of Jacob your father,
for the mouth of Yahweh has spoken.”

notes.text: Hebrew shofar.
Or “and exact all your debts.”
Luke 4:18 includes this line in Jesus’ reading in Nazareth, from the Septuagint, “to set at liberty those who are oppressed.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “with a garment.”
Or “shall be your rear guard”; compare 52:12.

verses.text:
Look, Yahweh’s arm is not too short to save,
and his ear is not too deaf to hear;

but your iniquities have made a division
between you and your God,
and your sins have hidden his face from you,
so that he does not hear.

Their threads shall not become a garment,
nor shall they clothe themselves with their handiwork.
Their doings are doings of iniquity,
and the work of violence is in their palms.

We roar, all of us, like bears,
and like doves we keep mourning;
we look for judgment, and there is none,
for deliverance, and it stays far off from us.

transgressing, and denying Yahweh,
and turning back from following our God,
speaking oppression and revolt,
conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.

Truth is gone,
and whoever turns from evil becomes a target.
Yahweh saw it, and it displeased him
that there was no justice.

He saw that there was no man,
and was astonished that none stepped in;
so his arm wrought deliverance for him,
and his own righteousness sustained him.

He put on righteousness like body armor,
and placed a helmet of salvation on his head;{d}
he put on clothes of vengeance
and wrapped himself in zeal like a cloak.

“And to Zion a Redeemer shall come,
and to them that turn from rebellion in Jacob,” declares Yahweh.{f}

“And as for me, this is my covenant with them,” says Yahweh: “My Spirit that is upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your offspring, nor out of the mouth of your offspring’s offspring,” says Yahweh,{g} “from this time forth and forevermore.”

notes.text: The Great Isaiah Scroll lacks this line; 1QIsa-b has it.
Paul quotes verses 7–8 in Romans 3:15–17.
The meaning of Hebrew ashmannim, “among the vigorous,” is uncertain.
Compare Ephesians 6:14, 17; 1 Thessalonians 5:8.
Or “when the enemy comes like a river, the Spirit of Yahweh lifts a banner against him.”
Paul quotes verses 20–21 in Romans 11:26–27 in a form close to the Septuagint, “the deliverer shall come for Zion’s sake, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob”; Paul has “from Zion.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll lacks this second “says Yahweh”; 1QIsa-b has it.

verses.text:
Get up, shine, for your light has arrived,
and Yahweh’s glory has dawned on you.

For see, darkness shall cover the earth,
and deep gloom the peoples;
but upon you Yahweh will rise,
and his glory shall be seen upon you.

And nations shall walk to your light,
and kings to the brightness of your dawning.

Then you will look and glow with joy;
your heart will pound and swell,
because the riches of the sea will be brought to you
and the wealth of nations will come to you.

Who are these that fly along as a cloud,
as doves to their lattices?

The coastlands are waiting for me,
with the ships of Tarshish in the lead,
bringing your children from far away,
together with their silver and gold,
to honor the name of Yahweh your God,
the Holy One of Israel,
for he has made you glorious.

Foreigners will rebuild your walls,
and their kings will serve you;
though in anger I struck you down,
in kindness I have shown you mercy.

The splendor of Lebanon will come to you,
its cypress, plane and pine trees together,
to adorn my sanctuary;
and I will honor the place where I rest my feet.

The sons of your oppressors
shall come to you bowed low,
and all that scorned you shall fall down at the soles of your feet;{e}
they shall call you the City of Yahweh,
the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

Instead of your being abandoned and hated,
so that none went through you,
I will make you an eternal pride,
the joy of generation after generation.

You will drink the milk of nations
and nurse at the breasts of kings;
then you will know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior
and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

Violence will no longer be heard of in your country,
or devastation and destruction inside your borders;
you will name your walls Salvation
and your gates Praise.

And your people, every one of them righteous,
shall inherit the land for all time,
the shoot of my planting, the work of my hands,
that I may be glorified.{h}

notes.text: Hebrew “nursed upon the side.”
Compare Matthew 2:11.
So the Great Isaiah Scroll (“and they shall go up for acceptance”); the Masoretic Text has “they shall go up on acceptance, my altar.”
Or “with their kings leading them”; compare Revelation 21:25–26.
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “all” before “the sons” and an erased word after it.

The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “by night”: “nor for brightness by night shall the moon give you light”; compare the Septuagint, “nor shall the rising of the moon lighten your night.” 1QIsa-b agrees with the Masoretic Text in lacking “by night.”
Or “your glory.” Compare Revelation 21:23; 22:5. 1QIsa-b is reported to end the verse at “everlasting light,” without this last line.
The written form of the Hebrew has “his planting.”

verses.text:
Strangers shall stand and shepherd your flocks;
foreigners shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers;

Their offspring shall be known among the nations,
and their descendants in the midst of the peoples;
all who see them shall acknowledge them,
that they are an offspring Yahweh has blessed.

For as the earth brings forth its growth,
and as a garden makes what is sown in it spring up,
so the Lord Yahweh will make righteousness and praise
spring up before all the nations.{j}

notes.text: The Great Isaiah Scroll reads “The Spirit of Yahweh,” without “Lord”; 1QIsa-b reads “The Spirit of Yahweh God” (Yahweh Elohim). The Septuagint has “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach good tidings to the poor.” Jesus reads verses 1–2a in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luke 4:18–19) in a form close to the Septuagint, and declares, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” For the anointed one (Hebrew mashiah), compare 11:2; 42:1; 45:1.

Hebrew peqah-qoah, “opening, opening,” perhaps “release” from the dark of prison (compare 42:7); the Great Isaiah Scroll writes it as one word. The Septuagint has “and recovery of sight to the blind,” which Luke 4:18 includes.
Jesus’ reading in Luke 4:19 stops before this line. Compare 34:8; 63:4.
There is a play on sound in the Hebrew: pe’er, “garland,” for efer, “ashes.”
Compare Exodus 19:6; 1 Peter 2:9; Revelation 1:6.
Or “and to their glory you shall succeed.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll has the second person, “instead of disgrace you shall rejoice in your portion … you shall possess a double portion; everlasting joy shall be yours.”
Or, with different vowels, “robbery with burnt offering.” The Septuagint has “robberies of injustice.”
Hebrew yekhahen pe’er, “acts as priest with a turban.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll reads “Yahweh God” for “the Lord Yahweh.”

verses.text:
Because of Zion I will not hold my peace,
and because of Jerusalem I will not rest,
till her righteousness shines out like the dawn,
and her salvation like a blazing torch.

You shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of Yahweh,
and a royal turban in the palm of your God.{b}

For as a youth weds a maiden,
your sons shall wed you;{g}
and with the joy of a bridegroom over his bride
your God shall rejoice over you.

I have posted guards on your walls,
Jerusalem;
they will never be quiet,
day or night.
You who remind Yahweh,
do not give yourselves any rest,

Yahweh has taken an oath by his right hand
and by the arm of his strength:
“I will not again give your grain
to be food for your enemies,
and the sons of foreigners shall not drink your new wine
for which you have toiled;

but those who gather it in shall eat it
and praise Yahweh,
and those who collect it shall drink it
in the courts of my sanctuary.”{i}

Look, Yahweh has announced
to the ends of the earth:
Tell Zion’s daughter,
“Look, your savior is coming;{k}
his reward comes with him,
and his payment goes before him.”

And they shall call them The Holy People,
The Redeemed of Yahweh;
and you shall be called Sought Out,
A City Not Forsaken.

notes.text: Compare 65:15; Revelation 2:17; 3:12.
The Great Isaiah Scroll lacks “and a turban.”
Hebrew Azuvah.
Hebrew Shemamah.
Hephzibah means “My Delight Is in Her”; it was also the name of King Manasseh’s mother (2 Kings 21:1).
Beulah means “Married.”
Or, with different vowels, “so shall your Builder marry you” (bonayikh for banayikh); compare 49:17; 54:13.
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “and until he sets up.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “says your God” at the end.
For the last line the Great Isaiah Scroll reads “clear away the stone of stumbling; say among the peoples.” 1QIsa-b agrees with the Masoretic Text.
Compare 40:10. Matthew 21:5 combines “Say to the daughter of Zion” with Zechariah 9:9.

verses.text:
Why is there red upon your clothing,
and your garments as of one treading the vat?

For a day of vengeance was in my heart,
and the year of my redeemed ones had arrived.

I will tell of Yahweh’s faithful acts of love
and his praiseworthy deeds,
all that Yahweh has done for us,
and the great kindness toward the house of Israel
that he showed them out of his mercy
and his abundant love.

But they rebelled
and grieved his Holy Spirit;{g}
so he turned to be their enemy,
and he himself fought against them.

who sent his glorious arm
to march at Moses’ right hand,
who divided the water in front of them
to make an everlasting name for himself,

who led them through the depths?
Like a horse in the open country,
they did not stumble.

Like livestock that go down into the valley,
the Spirit of Yahweh gave them rest.
So you led your people,
to make for yourself a glorious name.

Gaze down from heaven and behold,
from your dwelling of holiness and splendor.
Where is your zeal, and where your might?
The stirring of your inward parts and your compassion
are held back from me.

O Yahweh, why do you make us stray from your ways,
and make our heart hard against fearing you?
Turn back for your servants’ sake,
for the tribes that are your heritage.

For a little while your holy people possessed it;{k}
our adversaries have trampled down your sanctuary.

We have become like those over whom you have never ruled,
like those who were not called by your name.{l}

notes.text: Edom, “red”; compare Genesis 25:30. The figure of the bloodied warrior is taken up in Revelation 19:13–15.
Bozrah, a chief city of Edom; the name sounds like batsir, “grape harvest.”
Hebrew tso‘eh, “bending,” perhaps “striding”; with a slight change, “marching.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll lacks “I trod them in my anger … on my garments,” probably because the copyist’s eye skipped between similar words; 1QIsa-b has the lines. Compare Revelation 14:19–20; 19:15.
Many Hebrew manuscripts and the Targum are reported to read “I shattered them” (ashabberem) for “I made them drunk” (ashakkerem).

The written form of the Hebrew has “not” (lo’), the read form “to him” (lo); the written form may be taken “In all their distress he did not afflict” or, joined to the next line with the Septuagint, “not an envoy nor an angel, but his own presence saved them.” The Great Isaiah Scroll has neither word. The Septuagint reads “not an ambassador, nor a messenger, but himself saved them.”
Compare Ephesians 4:30.
Or “Then his people remembered the days of old, of Moses.”
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint has “the shepherd of the sheep.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “he” (“our Redeemer from of old, he is your name”).
Or “possessed your sanctuary.”
In the Hebrew text this verse continues with the line that English Bibles number 64:1.

verses.text:
If only you would rend the heavens and descend,
so that the mountains shook before you,{a}

as when fire sets brushwood ablaze
and fire makes the water boil,
to make your name known to your adversaries,
that the nations might tremble at your presence!

When you did fearful deeds we had not hoped for,
you descended; the mountains shook before you.{b}

Since ages past no one has heard,
no ear has caught it,
nor has eye beheld any God but you
who works on behalf of him who waits for him.{c}

We have all become like one who is unclean,
and all our righteous deeds are like a stained garment.{e}
We all wither like a leaf,
and our iniquities, like the wind, carry us away.

Be not angry beyond measure, O Yahweh,
nor remember iniquity forever.
See, look, we pray, we are all your people.

The house of our holiness and our splendor,
in which our fathers gave you praise,
is burned up with fire,
and every precious thing of ours is a ruin.

After all this, Yahweh, will you hold back?
Will you stay silent and punish us without limit?

notes.text: 64:1 is 63:19b in the Hebrew text, and Hebrew 64:1–11 is numbered 64:2–12 in English Bibles.
The Great Isaiah Scroll lacks “that we did not look for” (literally “we did not wait for”), reading “awesome things we waited for.”
Paul echoes this verse in 1 Corinthians 2:9.
The Hebrew of the last line is obscure. The Septuagint has “therefore we have erred.”
Hebrew beged ‘iddim, “a garment of menstruation,” that is, ritually unclean (Leviticus 15:19–24).
Hebrew wattemugenu, “and made us melt”; the Septuagint and other ancient versions are reported to read “and delivered us.”
Compare 29:16; 45:9; Jeremiah 18:6; Romans 9:20–21.

verses.text:
All day long I have held out my hands
to a rebellious people,
who walk a path that is not good,
following their own plans;{b}

a people who provoke me
to my face continually,
sacrificing in the gardens
and burning incense upon the bricks;{c}

who say, ‘Stand back by yourself,
draw not near to me, for I am holier than you.’{e}
Such men are smoke in my nose,
a fire burning all day long.

This is what Yahweh says:
“When juice is still found in a cluster of grapes,
and someone says, ‘Do not spoil it,
because there is something good in it,’
I will do the same for the sake of my servants
and not destroy everyone.

I will bring forth offspring from Jacob,
and from Judah heirs of my mountains;
my chosen ones shall inherit it,
and my servants shall dwell there.

“But you who forsake Yahweh,
who forget my holy mountain,
who set a table for Gad,
and fill bowls of mixed wine for Meni,{g}

see, my servants shall shout from a glad heart,
and you shall cry out from a sore heart,
and howl from a shattered spirit.

so that whoever asks for a blessing in the land
will ask the God of truth{h} for it,
and whoever takes an oath in the land
will swear by the God of truth;
for the earlier troubles will be forgotten
and hidden from my sight.

“For see, I create new heavens
and a new earth,{i}
and the former things shall not be remembered,
nor come into mind.

They shall build houses and dwell in them;
they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

Before they call I will answer;
while they are yet speaking I will hear.

notes.text: Paul quotes verses 1–2 from the Septuagint in Romans 10:20–21, applying verse 1 to the Gentiles and verse 2 to Israel.
Or “their own thoughts.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll reads obscurely “and they suck (?) hands upon the stones.”
Or “among the rock tombs.”
Hebrew “for I am holy to you,” or, with different vowels, “for I would make you holy,” that is, pass holiness on to you.
Achor, “trouble”; compare Joshua 7:24–26; Hosea 2:15.
Gad and Meni are pagan gods of luck, “Fortune” and “Destiny”; meni puns on manah, “destine,” in verse 12. The Septuagint has “a table for the devil … a drink offering to Fortune.”
Hebrew Elohe amen, “the God of truth,” “the faithful God.” Compare 2 Corinthians 1:20; Revelation 3:14.
Compare 66:22; 2 Peter 3:13; Revelation 21:1.
Compare Revelation 21:4.
Or “the youth shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner shall be accursed at a hundred years old”; either way, a life of a hundred years shall be thought short.
Compare 11:6–9; Genesis 3:14.

verses.text:
My hand made all these things,
and that is how they all came into being,
declares Yahweh.
But this is the person I will look at:
the one who is humble, broken in spirit,
and trembles at my word.

Hear the word of Yahweh,
you who tremble at his word:
“Your kinsmen that hate you,
that thrust you away because of my name,
have said, ‘Let Yahweh show his glory,
that we may see your joy’;
yet they themselves shall be ashamed.

Hark, a tumult from the city!
Hark, from the temple!
It is the voice of Yahweh,
rendering recompense to his enemies!

Who has heard such a thing?
Who has seen such things?
Shall a land be born in one day?
Shall a nation be brought forth in a moment?
For as soon as Zion was in labor
she brought forth her sons.

Would I bring a baby to the moment of birth and not deliver it?”
says Yahweh;
“would I, the one who delivers, close the womb?”
says your God.

For thus says Yahweh:
“Behold, I will make peace flow to her as a river,
and the riches of the nations as a stream in flood;
and you shall be nursed, and borne upon the side,
and dandled upon the knees.

“Look, Yahweh is coming with fire,
and his chariots are like a whirlwind,
to repay his anger with fury
and his rebuke with blazing flames.

“People who consecrate and cleanse themselves to enter the gardens,
following someone in the middle,{f}
and who eat pork, detestable creatures and mice,
will all meet their end together, declares Yahweh.

They will bring all your relatives from every nation
as an offering to Yahweh,
on horses, in chariots and wagons,
on mules and on camels,
to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says Yahweh,
as the Israelites bring grain offerings
in clean containers to Yahweh’s house.

And of them too I will take some
to be priests, to be Levites, says Yahweh.{i}

“As the new heavens and the new earth
that I am making
will stand before me, declares Yahweh,
so your descendants and your name will stand.

And it shall be that month by month at the new moon,
and week by week on the Sabbath,
all flesh shall come to bow down before me,
declares Yahweh.

notes.text: Stephen quotes verses 1–2a in Acts 7:49–50; compare 1 Kings 8:27.
Or “like one who worships wickedness” (aven, “trouble,” “idolatry”).
Compare Revelation 12:5.
Or “from the abundance of her glory”; the meaning of Hebrew ziz is uncertain.
The Great Isaiah Scroll reads “For with fire Yahweh shall come to judge … all flesh,” lacking the second “Yahweh.”

So the read form of the Hebrew, “one (feminine),” perhaps a priestess or goddess; the written form has the masculine. The Septuagint has “and eat swine’s flesh in the porches.” For “shall come to an end together, declares Yahweh,” the Great Isaiah Scroll reads “together, says Yahweh.”
The Hebrew is abrupt, “And I, their works and their thoughts …”; “knowing” is supplied.
Hebrew “who draw the bow.” For “Pul” the Septuagint has “Phud” (Put), and in place of “who draw the bow” it has “Meshech.”
The Great Isaiah Scroll adds “to me” (“for priests, for Levites to me”).

Jesus applies the last lines to Gehenna in Mark 9:48. In synagogue reading verse 23 is repeated after verse 24, so that the book does not end on a note of judgment; the Great Isaiah Scroll and 1QIsa-b end with verse 24 as in the Masoretic Text.
